dropped.why: pair breaking in Al needs phonons >= 2Delta = 99 GHz (Delta = 205 ueV, CITED); at r_C = 100 nm, x = q r_C = 15.6, kernel ~1e-101. No usable bound (DERIVED structural negative).

dropped.item: Low-threshold cryogenic detector spectra (SuperCDMS/CRESST/EDELWEISS/SENSEI/DAMIC), 30 eV - 10 keV
dropped.why: mass-proportional CSL at r_C = 100 nm makes no photons in neutral matter for E << 12.4 keV (Donadi 2021) and no phonons above ~37 GHz with lambda <= 1; detector rates therefore bound nothing in this parametrization. Same reason the LEE cannot be this effect.

dropped.item: Optical / IR / UV spontaneous emission from lab samples
dropped.why: same neutral-atom cancellation (lambda_k >> 0.1 nm). Only free charges radiate; covered via cosmic backgrounds (very weak).

dropped.item: Optical/UV extragalactic background and 13.6 eV - 1 keV
dropped.why: not converted this stage (EBL numbers not fetched; 13.6 eV - 0.3 keV absorbed by Galactic H I). Would give lambda ~ O(1) at best by the same model.

flags: Stage 33 suggested "low-threshold calorimeters staring at a cold massive sample (dGamma/dE ~ 1/E favours low energies)". That was wrong for neutral matter: below ~12.4 keV electrons and nucleus emit coherently and cancel (Donadi 2021). Corrected here.
IGEX band (Stage 33) starts at 14.5 keV where lambda_k = 0.086 nm, only just below the 0.1 nm atomic scale: the incoherent-electron assumption is marginal at its low edge.
Stage 33 assigned the white bulk-heating bound to its half-max band. Read band-limited (ccb18 Eq. 19) it is 4.02e-11 (1.30x weaker).

LEE coincidence: NOT a candidate. (i) structural: no eV-keV deposits in this parametrization; (ii) EXCESS: rates/shapes differ between detectors, decay with time, jump after warm-ups above 10 K - a stationary universal noise cannot do that.
Energy is not the discriminator: the EDELWEISS RED20 excess carries only ~2.0e-17 W/kg (0.2-1 keV), 2e-06 of the 10 pW/kg bulk residual.

donadi21.ref: Donadi, Piscicchia, Del Grande et al., "Novel CSL bounds from the noise-induced radiation emission from atoms", EPJC 81, 773 (2021), arXiv:2107.11237
donadi21.location: Sec. II p.5-6, Eq. (5); Appendix Eqs. (44)-(49)
donadi21.quote: "one needs to find a region where the wavelength of the emitted radiation lambda_k is small enough to guarantee that the electrons and the nucleus emit independently from each other, so that their contribution does not add coherently to zero, since they have opposite charges. Therefore one has to consider wavelengths lambda_k << 0.1 nm" ; "when the distance between two particles is larger than lambda_k the emission is always incoherent. On the other hand, particles at a distance smaller than lambda_k and rC always emit coherently" ; Eq. (44) "dGamma_t/dE = hbar lambda/(4 pi^2 eps0 c^3 m0^2 rC^2 E) Sum_i q_i^2" (incoherent)
